papers.title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
reasons: 🎯 temas: vuln & threats, AI agents, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: Human oversight is a pillar of AI safety. It is often exercised by a human in the loop (HITL) who approves critical actions taken by an AI agent. AI agents' increasing ability to bypass guardrails, though, raises the question of how to enforce HITL robustly. We introduce the concept of inalienable human-in-the-loop (I-HITL). An I-HITL protocol ensures that an agent can initiate an action only with explicit human approval, even when the human interacts with a system (e.g., a local agentic harness) compromised by the agent. A strong I-HITL protocol additionally ensures such approval even when an adversarial human attempts to delegate approvals to an agent. To motivate I-HITL, we report on experiments with a popular agentic wallet platform in which raising an agent's spending cap requires HITL approval via emailed one-time passcodes (OTPs). Given access to the user's email and a task blocked by the cap, we find that ten different frontier models will often autonomously raise the cap, harvesting OTPs to bypass a HITL guardrail and surfacing other vulnerabilities. We formally define I-HITL using the concept of communication topologies and prove necessary and sufficient conditions for its realization. We show that an I-HITL protocol requires a trusted entity - a trusted computing device (or equivalent) - and characterize which such devices can and cannot realize an I-HITL protocol. We present a prototype I-HITL system called Countersign that can plug into and strengthen existing HITL systems using off-the-shelf consumer mobile devices.

summary_es.tldr: Protege la supervisión humana en IA contra agentes maliciosos y humanos adversarios con un protocolo de aprobación inalienable.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes de IA pueden eludir las salvaguardas, incluso cuando la supervisión humana (HITL) está presente, y un humano adversario puede delegar aprobaciones a un agente, comprometiendo la seguridad.
summary_es.propuesta: Introduce el concepto de 'Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop' (I-HITL), un protocolo que exige aprobación humana explícita para acciones críticas, incluso si el sistema está comprometido o un humano intenta delegar la aprobación.
summary_es.resultados: Experimentos en una plataforma de billetera de IA mostraron que modelos de frontera a menudo eluden la supervisión HITL (aprobación por OTPs por correo electrónico) al cosechar OTPs. Se definen formalmente las condiciones para I-HITL y se demuestra que requiere un dispositivo de computación confiable.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Garantiza que la supervisión humana sea robusta y confiable, previniendo que agentes de IA o usuarios malintencionados socaven las medidas de seguridad críticas en sistemas de IA.

papers.title: Scope-Gap Injection: Exploiting Evaluator Channel Blind Spots in the OpenClaw Agent Security Competition
reasons: 🎯 temas: vuln & threats, LLM, AI agents
papers.abstract_en: This paper introduces Scope-Gap Injection (SGI), an indirect prompt injection method for multi-stage LLM-agent safety pipelines. In the IJCAI 2026 OpenClaw Agent Security Attack Competition, each attack package is judged by a static skill scan (S1), an LLM-judge safety check over the task and skill definition (S2), and a live execution audit (S3). Our observations suggest a scope gap: S2 appears to inspect the task instruction and skill definition without inspecting attachment contents, while the agent reads attachments during S3. SGI keeps the visible task and skill benign, while target identifiers, bypass parameters, and authorization procedures are moved into an attachment written as a business worklist. The S2 judge therefore sees a harmless task, while the agent follows the hidden worklist and triggers the permission bypass. In OpenClaw, SGI bypassed all three stages for 5 of 19 targets. The highest-scoring single submission achieved $F = 0.385$. Across the submission campaign, attachment placement was associated with higher aggregate S2 acceptance than in-skill placement: 78% versus 23%. We close with defenses that align evaluator scope with the channels available to the agent.

summary_es.tldr: Nueva técnica de inyección de prompts explota puntos ciegos en la evaluación de agentes LLM, eludiendo la seguridad en competiciones.
summary_es.problema: Los sistemas de seguridad para agentes LLM multi-etapa, como los de la competición OpenClaw, tienen 'puntos ciegos' donde el evaluador (LLM-judge) no inspecciona todo el contenido que el agente sí utiliza en ejecución (ej. adjuntos).
summary_es.propuesta: Se introduce Scope-Gap Injection (SGI), un método de inyección indirecta que oculta instrucciones maliciosas en adjuntos (ej. 'business worklist') que el LLM-judge ignora, pero el agente ejecuta.
summary_es.resultados: SGI eludió las 3 etapas de seguridad en 5 de 19 objetivos en OpenClaw. La mejor sumisión individual alcanzó F=0.385. La ubicación en adjuntos tuvo un 78% de aceptación en S2 vs 23% en la habilidad.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Demuestra una vulnerabilidad crítica en la evaluación de seguridad de agentes LLM, exigiendo alinear el alcance de los evaluadores con los canales de datos del agente para defensas efectivas.

papers.title: Steering for Safety, Hijacking for Profit: Trojan Threats in the LLM Activation Steering Supply Chain
papers.abstract_en: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into Web search, online recommendation, and intelligent decision-making, the third-party plugin ecosystem centered on model customization continues to grow. Among these, Steering Vectors guide model behavior by intervening in internal representations. However, the open plugin ecosystem also introduces new supply-chain security risks: malicious plugins can disguise themselves as having legitimate functionality and covertly manipulate outputs without significantly affecting model performance. Although this risk poses a real threat, the security issues of Steering plugins in the LLM supply-chain ecosystem still lack systematic research. This paper audits eight mainstream open-source Steering plugin libraries and reveals three structural vulnerabilities: insufficient distribution integrity verification, excessive plugin privileges, and missing runtime monitoring, which offers an attack surface for attackers. To investigate this threat, we propose a malicious plugin, IDH. Specifically, IDH designs a norm-gated mutually exclusive routing mechanism and proposes an information-decay inflection point localization method to automatically select the injection layer, thereby simultaneously achieving benign and malicious functions. To counter such threats, we propose a runtime defense framework, by suppressing anomalous activation interventions and orthogonalizing inter-layer trajectory. We evaluate IDH across five mainstream LLMs, using safety-refusal steering as the legitimate functionality and commercial recommendation manipulation as the hijack objective. Experiments covering six brands across three commercial domains demonstrate that IDH achieves an attack success rate (ASR) of up to 97.8% while preserving high refusal rates on harmful requests.

summary_es.tldr: Los plugins de LLM pueden ser secuestrados para fines maliciosos, pero existen defensas para protegerlos.
summary_es.problema: Los plugins de LLM, usados para guiar su comportamiento, presentan vulnerabilidades en su cadena de suministro que permiten a atacantes manipular sus salidas para beneficio propio, disfrazándose de funciones legítimas.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone un plugin malicioso (IDH) que utiliza un mecanismo de enrutamiento y un método de localización de puntos de inflexión para inyectar funciones benignas y maliciosas simultáneamente. Como defensa, se introduce un marco de defensa en tiempo de ejecución que suprime intervenciones anómalas y ortogonaliza trayectorias.
summary_es.resultados: El plugin IDH logró una tasa de éxito de ataque (ASR) de hasta el 97.8% en cinco LLMs principales, manteniendo altas tasas de rechazo para solicitudes dañinas, en dominios comerciales como búsqueda web y recomendaciones.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Garantiza la seguridad de los sistemas basados en LLM, protegiendo contra la manipulación de salidas y el robo de información en aplicaciones críticas como la toma de decisiones y la recomendación online.

papers.title: JANUS: Synthesizing Cross-Layer Defenses Against Web Deserialization Attacks
papers.abstract_en: Unsafe deserialization turns untrusted data into attacker-controlled execution, and a single vulnerability can admit diverse exploit variants that evade defenses tailored to a known exploit. Existing defenses typically operate at a single enforcement point with limited visibility into the full attack. Combining controls across layers offers complementary protection, but coordinating them to preserve legitimate functionality and adapting them to new variants requires substantial expert effort. We propose JANUS, a red-blue adversarial framework for automated cross-layer defense synthesis. Starting from a known exploit, \sys iteratively refines deployment-specific policies in an isolated offline environment. A black-box attacker probes the current policy for exploit variants using only externally observable feedback. The defender summarizes each verified variant into its security-relevant effects, uses counterfactual replay to separate complementary coverage from redundant enforcement, and jointly selects and scopes controls across layers. Each candidate policy is validated against accumulated exploits and benign workflows. We evaluate JANUS on sixteen vulnerability deployments across six Java and PHP applications against gateway, application, system, and cross-layer defenses. JANUS reduces held-out attack success to 6.2%, compared with 18.8-55.0% for the baselines, fully mitigates 13 of 16 deployments, and preserves 98.4% of benign functionality tests at a 6.9% targeted P95 latency increase.

summary_es.tldr: JANUS automatiza la creación de defensas multicapa contra ataques de deserialización web, mejorando la seguridad y preservando la funcionalidad.
summary_es.problema: Los ataques de deserialización insegura son difíciles de defender porque una sola vulnerabilidad puede generar múltiples variantes de exploit que evaden las defensas existentes, las cuales suelen operar en un solo punto y tienen visibilidad limitada.
summary_es.propuesta: JANUS es un marco de defensa y ataque adversarial que sintetiza automáticamente defensas a través de múltiples capas. Utiliza un atacante de caja negra para encontrar variantes de exploit y un defensor que refina políticas de control (gateway, aplicación, sistema) para cubrir nuevas amenazas sin afectar la funcionalidad legítima.
summary_es.resultados: JANUS reduce el éxito de los ataques al 6.2% (vs 18.8-55.0% de los métodos base), mitiga completamente 13 de 16 despliegues, y preserva el 98.4% de la funcionalidad benigna con un aumento de latencia del 6.9%.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite a las organizaciones defenderse de manera más efectiva y automatizada contra ataques de deserialización web complejos, reduciendo el riesgo de compromiso y minimizando el impacto en el rendimiento de las aplicaciones.

papers.title: Then there is prompt injection, a malicious email, ...: The Wild Wide West of OpenClaw Agentic System Security
reasons: 🎯 temas: LLM, AI agents, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: AI-powered personal assistant frameworks such as OpenClaw combine LLM reasoning, persistent memory, tool invocation, local execution, and web-based workflows. These capabilities enable useful automation, but they also create security risks when untrusted inputs, model reasoning, tools, memory, and deployment configuration interact without explicit trust boundaries. This paper presents an empirical study of reported security concerns in OpenClaw using two complementary data sources: Reddit discussions and security-tagged GitHub issues. We analyze more than 25K Reddit posts from 13 OpenClaw-related subreddits and identify 162 security-relevant posts with 1,787 associated comments. We further collect 358 security-tagged GitHub issues and retain 180 issues describing concrete security concerns. Using qualitative analysis and evidence-grounded CWE mapping, we identify 521 CWE instances across 59 distinct weakness types, concentrated in access-control failures, sensitive-data exposure, injection, and unsafe execution. We also extract 543 practitioner mitigation suggestions and consolidate them into seven recurring strategies. To complement the empirical analysis, we present an evidence-grounded illustrative reconstruction of a representative sensitive-data exposure pathway using dummy secret values. Our findings show that OpenClaw security issues are not isolated implementation bugs; they reflect recurring trust-boundary failures across the agent execution pipeline. We discuss how these weaknesses map to both traditional software-security categories and agent-specific failure mechanisms, and derive implications for safer agentic systems, including explicit trust boundaries, least-privilege tool access, execution containment, runtime oversight, and defense-in-depth deployment.

summary_es.tldr: Los asistentes IA como OpenClaw presentan riesgos de seguridad por fallos en los límites de confianza, afectando a control de acceso, datos sensibles y ejecución.
summary_es.problema: Los marcos de asistentes IA como OpenClaw, que combinan razonamiento LLM, memoria persistente y ejecución de herramientas, crean riesgos de seguridad al interactuar sin límites de confianza explícitos entre entradas no confiables, razonamiento del modelo, herramientas, memoria y configuración de despliegue.
summary_es.propuesta: Se realizó un estudio empírico de las preocupaciones de seguridad reportadas en OpenClaw analizando discusiones en Reddit y problemas de GitHub etiquetados como de seguridad. Se identificaron debilidades y se mapearon a categorías CWE, además de extraer sugerencias de mitigación de los profesionales.
summary_es.resultados: Se analizaron más de 25K posts de Reddit y 358 issues de GitHub, identificando 162 posts y 180 issues relevantes. Se encontraron 521 instancias de CWE en 59 tipos de debilidades, concentradas en fallos de control de acceso, exposición de datos sensibles, inyección y ejecución insegura. Se extrajeron 543 sugerencias de mitigación consolidadas en siete estrategias.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Los problemas de seguridad en OpenClaw no son errores aislados, sino fallos recurrentes en los límites de confianza a lo largo del pipeline de ejecución del agente. Esto tiene implicaciones directas para el diseño de sistemas de agentes más seguros, requiriendo límites de confianza explícitos, acceso a herramientas con mínimo privilegio, contención de ejecución y defensa en profundidad.

papers.title: The Target Agent Is Its Own Best Critic but a Poor Proposer: Self-Improved Red Teaming
papers.abstract_en: Automatic red teaming increasingly relies on large language models (LLMs) to iteratively diagnose failed attacks and propose improved adversarial prompts or injections. Although prior work strengthens this loop through prompt engineering and search-harness design, the mechanisms underlying its two core roles, criticism and attack proposal, has not been explored. To further investigate the core roles and therefore improve red teaming effectiveness, we disentangle two design choices: whether criticism is generated by the target session itself (self-criticism) or by a separately instantiated critic (external criticism), and whether that criticism is translated into the next attack by the target session (self-proposal) or by a separate attacker (external proposal). Through our analysis, we find that self-criticism is more effective because it is grounded in the target's live execution context, including observations, constraints, and available reasoning; removing reasoning reduces downstream attack success by 6%-17%. In contrast, self-proposal is substantially less effective because awareness of the adversarial objective induces explicit refusal and non-refusal sandbagging. These findings motivate a role-separated red-teaming approach: the target session diagnoses why an attack failed, while a separately instantiated attacker generates the next proposal. On DTAP-BENCH, spanning Telecom, Workflow, CRM, and Code domains, under both direct misuse and indirect threat models, as well as multiple agent frameworks, this configuration achieves 63.2% overall attack success rate (ASR), much higher than baselines. Our results show that effective automatic red teaming depends not only on model capability and search strategy, but also on how execution context and adversarial responsibility are distributed across model sessions.

summary_es.tldr: La autocrítica mejora el red teaming automático al usar el contexto del objetivo, pero la autopropuesta falla; la separación de roles es clave.
summary_es.problema: Los métodos actuales de red teaming automático con LLMs no exploran suficientemente los roles de crítica y propuesta de ataques, limitando su efectividad.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone un enfoque de red teaming con roles separados: el modelo objetivo realiza la autocrítica basada en su contexto de ejecución, mientras que un atacante separado genera la propuesta de ataque.
summary_es.resultados: La autocrítica mejora el éxito del ataque en un 6-17% al estar anclada en el contexto. La autopropuesta es menos efectiva. La configuración de roles separados logra un 63.2% de éxito general en DTAP-BENCH.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Comprender la distribución del contexto de ejecución y la responsabilidad del atacante es crucial para mejorar la efectividad del red teaming automático y la seguridad de los sistemas de IA.

papers.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
reasons: 🎯 temas: vuln & threats, LLM, AI agents
papers.abstract_en: A vulnerability costs more to fix the later it is discovered. As coding agents generate code faster than developers can review it, software needs a first line of defense screening each new function in real time. LLM agents have recently become capable of finding real-world vulnerabilities by working as a security expert would: they run analysis tools, explore the surrounding code, test hypotheses and weigh the evidence before forming their own judgement. This reasoning, however, spans many model calls, so that each verdict takes minutes of compute, far too long for real-time screening. Faster detectors, which fine-tune deep learning models or prompt an LLM for a direct verdict, are less accurate: they judge a function without the context an agent gathers, and an LLM's generated verdict is unreliable even when given some of it. We present REVA (REal-time Vulnerability Analysis), an AI vulnerability detector that brings the security context and code understanding components behind agentic detectors into a single forward pass of an LLM. For each new function, REVA gives the LLM a pre-computed threat model of its module, lightweight static analysis findings and call-graph information. REVA leverages a trained probe to read the LLM's internal representations of the new function in this context. On PrimeVul's held-out test set, REVA on GLM-5.3-Flash reaches 60.0% accuracy in about one second per function. This matches VulTriage (59.2%), the state-of-the-art agentic detector, run on the same LLM, while being over 250 times faster and less than a tenth as costly. On the same prompt, the probe is 14% to 17% more accurate than the LLM's own direct verdict. Across three open LLMs, REVA is at least as accurate as VulTriage, and about 10% more accurate on two of them. An LLM's internal representations thus encode much of what agentic detectors obtain through reasoning.

summary_es.tldr: REVA detecta vulnerabilidades en código en tiempo real, combinando análisis contextual y la inteligencia de los LLMs de forma eficiente.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes de IA que detectan vulnerabilidades en código son lentos (minutos por función), lo que impide su uso en tiempo real para revisar el código generado rápidamente por otros agentes de IA.
summary_es.propuesta: REVA integra el contexto de seguridad y el análisis de código (modelo de amenazas, hallazgos de análisis estático, grafo de llamadas) en una sola pasada del LLM, utilizando una sonda entrenada para leer las representaciones internas del modelo.
summary_es.resultados: REVA alcanza un 60.0% de precisión en ~1 segundo por función en el conjunto de pruebas de PrimeVul, igualando al detector agentic VulTriage (59.2%) pero siendo 250 veces más rápido y menos costoso. La sonda de REVA es un 14-17% más precisa que el veredicto directo del LLM.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite la detección de vulnerabilidades de seguridad en tiempo real durante el desarrollo de software, mejorando la seguridad y reduciendo costos al identificar fallos tempranamente.

papers.title: CoSA: The Conflict of Skills Attack in Real-World LLM Agent Ecosystems
papers.abstract_en: Agent Skills allow LLM agents to combine reusable capabilities, but checking each Skill in isolation cannot rule out policy violations when they are composed. We term such failures Conflict of Skills (CoS): artifacts or assessment signals produced for one purpose may be reused downstream without preserving the restrictions or authorization needed for their new use. Using controlled executions of publicly available Skills and matched single-Skill controls, we identify four recurring mechanisms behind CoS. Building on these findings, we introduce the Conflict of Skills Attack (CoSA), which adds locally admitted Skills to an existing pool to supply missing business operations (capability supplementation) or reshape artifact exchange, decision reuse, and target/action bindings (relationship reshaping). CoSA leaves existing Skills and runtime permissions unchanged. To evaluate this threat under autonomous Skill selection, we introduce CoSA-Bench, built from real-world Skills and controlled services, with 288 tasks across recruiting, finance, IT, and business, covering data leakage, unauthorized state modification, and unsafe execution. Across five LLMs and three agent harnesses, additions capped at 5% of each original pool raise the policy-violation rate from 35.02% to 58.45%, an increase of 23.43 percentage points. Trace analysis links compliant-to-violating transitions to cross-Skill dependencies involving the additions. Finally, we develop a lightweight harness-level guard that checks information flow and authorization before consequential actions. On OpenClaw recruiting tasks across five models, the guard reduces violations from 65.28% to 6.67%, while policy-compliant task completion on matched benign controls changes from 66.67% to 65.00%.

summary_es.tldr: El ataque CoSA explota la composición de habilidades en agentes LLM para eludir políticas de seguridad, afectando ecosistemas reales.
summary_es.problema: Las políticas de seguridad de los agentes LLM no se aplican correctamente cuando se componen múltiples habilidades reutilizables, llevando a violaciones de políticas (Conflict of Skills).
summary_es.propuesta: Se introduce el ataque CoSA, que añade habilidades maliciosas a un conjunto existente para complementar operaciones o reconfigurar el intercambio de artefactos y la ejecución de acciones, sin modificar permisos existentes.
summary_es.resultados: La adición de habilidades en un 5% a un conjunto existente incrementó la tasa de violación de políticas del 35.02% al 58.45% (un aumento de 23.43 puntos porcentuales) en CoSA-Bench. Un guardia propuesto redujo las violaciones del 65.28% al 6.67% en tareas de reclutamiento.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Demuestra una vulnerabilidad crítica en la composición de habilidades de agentes LLM, afectando la seguridad en aplicaciones prácticas y requiriendo nuevos mecanismos de defensa.

papers.title: Thinking-in-Bets at Test Time Reduces Sycophantic Revisions in LLM Agents
papers.abstract_en: Language model agents often abandon correct work when a user challenges it, yet simply telling them to stand firm makes them ignore real mistakes. Once an agent reads a complaint, it tends to discount its own earlier checks in order to agree with the user. We introduce Thinking-in-Bets, a training-free method in which an agent writes a short private record of its main claims, the checks supporting them, and its confidence before reading user feedback. When challenged, the agent consults this Claim Checklist to keep verified work intact while investigating uncertain or newly challenged parts. We evaluate five Gemini models (3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.5 Flash, 3.6 Flash, 3.8 Flash, and 4.0 Argon) across eight benchmarks: SWE-Together, SWE-Interact, and DeepSWE for software engineering, Agents' Last Exam for professional reports, Humanity's Last Exam and SycEval for academic reasoning, Vals Finance for financial analysis, and Terminal-Bench for command-line tasks. Recording claims before criticism nearly eliminates false reversals in patch review and protects passing report drafts under mistaken pushback, whereas writing the same record after reading the complaint recovers very little of the gain. In multi-turn coding, pre-reply claim records substantially reduce unnecessary file edits after mistaken complaints, and gating the record so it is written only when the agent is uncertain lowers token overhead while fixing more real bugs than the baseline. Even in non-interactive tasks without user feedback, listing the key claims in a draft and re-checking the weakest one before submission improves both answer accuracy and confidence estimates across all tested models.

summary_es.tldr: Los agentes de LLM ahora pueden defender su trabajo correcto contra críticas infundadas sin ignorar errores reales.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes de LLM a menudo descartan su propio trabajo correcto cuando un usuario los desafía, pero decirles que se mantengan firmes los hace ignorar errores reales.
summary_es.propuesta: Introduce 'Thinking-in-Bets', un método sin entrenamiento donde el agente registra sus afirmaciones principales, las verificaciones de apoyo y su confianza antes de leer la retroalimentación del usuario. Al ser desafiado, consulta este registro para mantener el trabajo verificado e investigar partes inciertas o recién desafiadas.
summary_es.resultados: Se eliminan casi por completo las reversiones falsas en la revisión de código y se protegen borradores de informes válidos bajo críticas erróneas. En codificación multi-turno, se reducen sustancialmente las ediciones innecesarias de archivos después de quejas erróneas. Incluso en tareas no interactivas, listar las afirmaciones clave y volver a verificar la más débil mejora la precisión de la respuesta y las estimaciones de confianza.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Este método mejora la fiabilidad y robustez de los agentes LLM, haciéndolos más útiles en aplicaciones prácticas al evitar que descarten trabajo correcto o realicen cambios innecesarios.

papers.title: Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents
papers.abstract_en: Continual learning is the ability of LLM agents to improve over time by acquiring, refining, and applying knowledge from experience while retaining useful prior knowledge. It is essential for agents learning over long time horizons, yet current evaluations largely assess individual task performance rather than improvement through accumulated experience. We introduce Continual Learning Exam (CLE), a large-scale benchmark developed by 50+ domain experts to measure experience-driven improvement in realistic professional workflows. CLE comprises 120 human-authored tasks, each organised as a five-level ladder, yielding 600 levels spanning 89 professional roles across 12 occupational domains. Agents must pass each level to unlock the next, with later levels building on experience accumulated during earlier assignments. An evaluation agent assesses each submission against human-authored rubrics. We compare a single-submission setting with one that provides diagnostic feedback after failure and allows one revision. Across 17 harness-model configurations using frontier LLMs, feedback and revision yield a median completion gain of 5.3 percentage points. Yet the best-performing system clears only 47.7% of levels and completes all five levels in just 23.3% of tasks, highlighting the difficulty of sustained learning from experience for existing frontier LLMs. As such, the dataset can also be used to post-train LLMs to strengthen their continual learning capabilities.

summary_es.tldr: Nuevo benchmark para evaluar la mejora continua de agentes LLM en tareas complejas y de largo plazo.
summary_es.problema: Las evaluaciones actuales de agentes LLM no miden adecuadamente su mejora a través de la experiencia acumulada en flujos de trabajo realistas y de largo plazo.
summary_es.propuesta: Se introduce Continual Learning Exam (CLE), un benchmark a gran escala con 120 tareas en 5 niveles, diseñado para medir la mejora impulsada por la experiencia en 89 roles profesionales.
summary_es.resultados: Los agentes con retroalimentación y una revisión mejoran un 5.3% en promedio, pero el mejor sistema solo completa el 47.7% de los niveles, demostrando la dificultad del aprendizaje continuo.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite evaluar y mejorar la capacidad de los LLM para aprender y adaptarse de forma continua en entornos profesionales complejos, crucial para su aplicación práctica a largo plazo.

papers.title: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as the primary paradigm for optimizing Large Language Model (LLM) agents, yet efficient critic-free algorithms (e.g., GRPO) suffer from a fundamental uniform credit assignment dilemma that broadcasts trajectory-level advantages equally to all actions. Our analysis reveals that this uniformity inherently reinforces structurally unreasonable actions in preferred trajectories and ignores each action's downstream deviations in unpreferred ones. To resolve this without introducing critic overhead, we propose Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping (ProAS), a plug-and-play framework that leverages a dynamically evolving Agentic Reference Graph (ARG) to achieve fine-grained credit assignment via Masking Unreasonable Incentives (MUI) and Asymmetric Penalty Redistribution (APR). Extensive experiments across Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct demonstrate that ProAS universally elevates mainstream group-based baselines to new state-of-the-art performance, achieving peak success rates of 91.9% and 94.3% on ALFWorld, alongside 66.7% and 70.8% on WebShop, respectively. Furthermore, it accelerates training convergence by up to $2.44\times$ while maintaining strong robustness against imperfect or distilled ARGs. Codes: https://github.com/LINs-lab/ProAS

summary_es.tldr: ProAS mejora el aprendizaje por refuerzo de agentes LLM asignando crédito de forma más inteligente a las acciones, sin necesidad de un crítico.
summary_es.problema: Los algoritmos de aprendizaje por refuerzo para agentes LLM (sin crítico) asignan el crédito de forma uniforme a todas las acciones en una trayectoria, lo que puede reforzar acciones erróneas y pasar por alto el impacto real de las acciones.
summary_es.propuesta: Proponemos ProAS, un framework 'plug-and-play' que utiliza un Grafo de Referencia del Agente (ARG) dinámico para asignar crédito de forma más granular. Emplea 'Masking Unreasonable Incentives' (MUI) y 'Asymmetric Penalty Redistribution' (APR) para ajustar la asignación de recompensas.
summary_es.resultados: ProAS mejora los modelos Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct y Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, alcanzando tasas de éxito del 91.9% y 94.3% en ALFWorld, y del 66.7% y 70.8% en WebShop. Acelera la convergencia del entrenamiento hasta 2.44x y es robusto ante ARGs imperfectos.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite entrenar agentes LLM más eficientes y efectivos en tareas complejas, reduciendo el tiempo de entrenamiento y mejorando el rendimiento sin aumentar la complejidad computacional con un crítico.

papers.title: Build, Don't Play: Self-Improving LLM Research Agents Develop a Hearthstone Battlegrounds AI That Rivals Top Players
papers.abstract_en: Can LLM agents carry a hard real-world problem from raw data to a system that holds its own against people? We study this in Hearthstone Battlegrounds, an eight-player auto-battler with stochastic shops and battles, hidden information and nearly a thousand interacting cards. We present AutoTavern, a self-improving research system: specialised LLM research agents share a typed research memory, every claim passes verification gates, and live games close the loop, so the agents improve the simulator, opponents and policy and, from the same feedback, their own research process; a human sets goals and rules on ambiguous mechanics. In 20 days AutoTavern built TavernGym, the first faithful, full-content reproduction of the live game, and delivered 23 versions of TavernAgent, trained with PPO against opponents calibrated to real games. TavernAgent plays complete games on the live ladder by itself: its rating rose from 6,000 to about 15,000 and, on the public leaderboard's measure, its last 20 records average a placement of 1.60 with 80% first places, better than the server's ten highest-rated players on every statistic (2.34, 59%). TavernBench, 960 tasks in 40 scenarios, shows that the system the agents built is the strongest player: TavernAgent answers 91% of the play tasks against at most 63% for frontier LLMs, and decides in 0.03 s where they need up to 26 s; within the second a live turn allows, it keeps 90% and no LLM more than 26%. LLM agents build far better than they play. We will open-source TavernBench and TavernGym at https://github.com/MCG-NJU/AutoTavern.

summary_es.tldr: Agentes LLM auto-mejorables desarrollan una IA para Hearthstone que supera a los mejores jugadores humanos en 20 días.
summary_es.problema: Investigar si los agentes LLM pueden resolver problemas complejos del mundo real, desde datos brutos hasta un sistema competitivo, en este caso una IA para Hearthstone Battlegrounds.
summary_es.propuesta: Se presenta AutoTavern, un sistema de investigación con agentes LLM especializados que comparten memoria, validan afirmaciones, y aprenden de partidas en vivo para mejorar el simulador, oponentes y su propia política de juego. Un humano define objetivos y reglas.
summary_es.resultados: En 20 días, AutoTavern creó TavernGym (una réplica del juego) y 23 versiones de TavernAgent. La IA alcanzó una calificación de ~15,000 (desde 6,000), logrando un promedio de 1.60 en la clasificación pública y un 80% de primeros puestos, superando a los 10 mejores jugadores en todas las estadísticas. TavernAgent resuelve el 91% de las tareas de juego contra un máximo del 63% de otros LLMs.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Demuestra que los agentes LLM pueden construir sistemas complejos y de alto rendimiento de forma autónoma, superando incluso a los expertos humanos en tareas específicas, lo que sugiere un futuro donde la IA no solo juega, sino que crea y mejora sistemas.
